title: Day 10 of the following month: early and late invoice dates
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A customer on the shop's own term due on the 10th of the following month is invoiced early and late in October.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due on day 10 of the following month.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-03 Customer and {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-03 Tenth.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15440.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Oct 28, 2026.
  4. Set Invoice Date to Oct 10, 2026.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice preview shows Invoice Date and Due date.
  • Step 2: the Due date reads Nov 10, 2026 (day 10 of November).
  • Step 3: the Due date reads Nov 10, 2026 (still day 10 of November, whatever the invoice day).
  • Step 4: the Due date reads Nov 10, 2026 (an invoice on day 10 is due in the following month, not the same day).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R2: “A "day of the following month" term is always due in the month after the invoice date, whatever the day of the invoice: with day 10, an invoice dated Oct 5 and one dated Oct 28 are both due Nov 10.”
  • Terminology: “The shop's own term → A term the shop created on the Credit Terms page, of one of two kinds: Due Net X days (due X days after the invoice date) or Due day of the following month (due on day X of the month after the invoice date).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "9 Invoice due date" ("10th of next month: invoice Oct 5, due Nov 10", "Invoice Oct 28: still due Nov 10"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

The design's own words:

  • “Always the next month, even when the 10th of this month is still ahead or nearly here. Day 31 in a 30-day month uses its last day (Nov 30).”
